acceptanceCases.case: THE MINT: a freshly generated settlement carries npc:<n> / inst:<n> / fac:<n> on every NPC, institution and faction — complete, unique within its kind, and 1-based contiguous.
⛔ SAME SEED, SAME IDS: two generations at one seed produce identical ids for every entity — the property EM-B2a's layer keys rest on.
⛔ A RENAME DOES NOT MOVE AN ID: renaming a faction and an institution leaves both ids unchanged — the direct negative control for `faction.${slug(name)}` and for name-keyed institution lookup.
⛔ A ROSTER EDIT DOES NOT RE-POINT AN ID: removing the second of five NPCs leaves the remaining four with their original ids, none renumbered — the direct negative control for `npc_${idx+1}`.
⛔ THE MINT TAKES NO DRAW: the golden corpus before and after, compared field by field except the new id keys, shows no value, count, name or ordering moving anywhere.

MIGRATION BACK-FILL AND IDEMPOTENCY: an older save with no ids gets them on its first read through the REAL saves path, in stored array order; the second read is byte-identical; the input is not mutated.

⛔ THE MIGRATION IS UNCONDITIONAL: a source scan proves the v3 arm is reached on every save read and write path and sits inside NO conditional, flag read or env read; SCHEMA_VERSION is still 1 and listMigrations() still holds ONE entry.

⛔ FOREIGN IDS AND THE RECORDED ASYMMETRY: an imported entity's non-matching id is LEFT ALONE and reported FOREIGN, never rewritten; and a save whose roster was reordered before migration has ids stable across later reads, with the test stating in its own words that they need not match a fresh generation's.
